pr_body:
This is a port of @lawnjelly's

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/76252/

to the master branch. It also takes bits
- from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/b287f970dd34d59b8ea9fe6150e76b1c5777423d (before the hierarchical culling in 3.x),
- from the preceding 3D PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/52846 as needed,
- and from the later fixup PRs.

TODO:

- [x] Resolve questions marked by `TODO` in the code
- [x] Check snapping code
- [x] TileMap
- [x] Documentation (and mention that this only works for 2D for now)

Left for a follow-up PR (if it is acceptable):

- CPUParticles2D

Thanks to @lawnjelly for the original PR.

- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/64182

Testing welcome! Make sure to enable the project setting `physics/common/physics_interpolation` and set `physics/common/physics_jitter_fix` to `0.0` when testing.

This PR is sponsored by My Spare Time™
pr_comments:
Great work @rburing . This is something I was not looking forward to :grin: as I'm not so familiar with master and there will inevitably be a lot of 4.x specific bugs / ongoing maintenance work.

Particles in particular have the potential to be tricky because (at least in 3.x) they were previously not specified in world space. They (and MultiMesh which CPUParticles used under the hood) were the most time consuming feature in 3.x, though more so for 3D.

Also we should pay particularly attention at whether CPUParticles are planned to be deprecated in 4.x (in which case you will have to get them working with GPUParticles). Also I noted that, at least in 3D, particles in 4.x already use some kind of interpolation so you will need to get both systems to play nice with each other.

Also as I noted above there may end up being some rejigging for snapping purposes. This is something I'm anticipating may need adjustment in 3.x based on feedback, as we haven't yet released 3.6. So in some ways this code may get more testing in 4.x (also bearing in mind there are now many more users on 4.x than 3.x). The paradigm is intended to be that transforms are interpolated and passed through the tree _without snapping_, and snapping is applied on a per object basis. Consider if a child node has a scaling applied, then trying to interpolate from snapped parent transforms would look incorrect otherwise.

BTW an option (if other reviewers are agreeable to this) that I used in 3.x is to leave particles to a followup PR. They will probably have a lot more bikeshedding / bugs, and it makes it easier to review both sections in depth. This does mean that realistically users will have to wait for particle PR to make finished games, but it does mean they can start testing etc more rapidly.

> Also I noted that, at least in 3D, particles in 4.x already use some kind of interpolation so you will need to get both systems to play nice with each other.

Only GPU particles have built-in interpolation in 4.x, and [it's not complete yet](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/51318).

Thanks for the feedback @lawnjelly ! I think it makes sense to leave particles for a follow-up PR, if reviewers can agree.

I'll have to look at the snapping (propagation) more carefully, and I'll ask for some more eyes on this on RocketChat.

The latest push also fixes this issue with TileMaps:


https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/229837/9f511cad-e07c-48ee-8be6-af340bd62975

The test from the project [PixelPerfectTest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/13244300/PixelPerfectTest.zip) from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/84380 seems to pass with a physics tick rate of 30 (also lower ones) plus the interpolation from this PR, after commenting out the `_process` function in `Camera.gd` (it was setting the camera position in both `_process` and `_physics_process`):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/229837/956bfec4-04ce-45f9-9ced-eddc8e76dcbf

This was recorded using Peek because movie writer mode is bugged when using the settings of the test project.

The potential issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/88424#discussion_r1493281555 with propagating snapped transforms to children should be present in `master` as well, so I'd prefer not to change the behavior in this PR. What would an MRP look like @lawnjelly? It can be reported separately.

> It's easy to make physics interpolation the default (should it also be a basic setting then?)

I'm not sure if it should be made a basic setting, considering we want to encourage leaving physics interpolation enabled as much as possible. In the long run, physics interpolation is something you should only disable for troubleshooting, or for games intended to run at a fixed framerate (which is generally a bad idea, but can minimize input lag in this particular situation).

> Consider if a child node has a scaling applied, then trying to interpolate from snapped parent transforms would look incorrect otherwise.

I've finally had a chance to test this (sorry was away from home when writing originally so was working from memory), and it doesn't seem to cause the problem that I envisaged, because the scaling turns out to be applied _after_ the translation. (The problem I was thinking of was e.g. moving parent node by 0.9 pixels, then child being scaled 10x and this movement being lost, when it should have moved 9 pixels.) But this was based on the incorrect assumption of scaling being applied first, so it seems fine so far in some tests. :+1:

Now I've had a look through, it looks pretty straightforward and good to me, and testing seems to be okay so far. The 4.x reviewers might have some preferences for cosmetic changes to naming etc.

One cosmetic thing to pay attention to might be the `physics_interpolation_mode` on Nodes - deciding whether to put it in a tab / group or have it out on its own. It made sense in 3.x, but imo it's easy to bog down the inspector properties with "cognitive overload" (especially for base classes), so hiding things in tabs (groups) can be helpful, and thinking ahead so similarish things can be grouped together in future is usually a good plan.

I fixed the overzealous internal process mode updates when setting a Camera2D to current, and the documentation.

Left to decide:

- [x] Enable physics interpolation by default or not? (Also considering the jitter fix setting and 3D.) No.
- [x] Put the physics interpolation mode property in its own group or not? Yes.

Left to do:

- [x] Get feedback from @godotengine/rendering about the remaining TODOs in the code (particularly about threading).

> Get feedback from @godotengine/rendering about the remaining TODOs in the code (particularly about threading).

I wouldn't excessively worry about `set_physics_interpolation_mode()` at this stage as it is likely to be a one off in most cases (unless it proves a problem).

`update_interpolation_tick()` is single threaded, it assumes that all the calls to `set_transform()` have occurred by that point (or will occur after, when syncing the physics). Have look where this is called in `main::iteration()`. Having a block synchronisation like this is much preferable if we can, otherwise you would need e.g. a mutex around each update to the interpolation lists.

If users are updating canvas items in multiple threads, the `set_transforms()` should get stored on a queue in the visual server (and updated sequentially), therefore hopefully no need for mutex there. But I'm assuming things here work same as 3.x. If you do some stress testing in multithreaded mode (with asan) this should help reveal if anything is treading on toes.

Essentially it's pretty easy to add e.g. mutexes, but hopefully can be avoided. You could add them temporarily and call `try_lock()` and report any cases of contention.

> Enable physics interpolation by default or not? (Also considering the jitter fix setting and 3D.)

Even if the final intention is to have this on by default, just to point out:

* It won't be fully usable until particle interpolation is also implemented. Particles may not look great when used in combination, and you may get strange particle glitches. As such this PR is a "preview".
* It will break existing games that move objects in `_process()`. They will probably look awful (and you may wish later to emit warnings for this case, as is currently done when detected when using 3D physics interpolation in 3.x. I haven't added warnings yet for 2D.).

I also personally don't always recommend using physics interpolation for some pixel based retro games as you can get e.g. "staggering" where object movement gets out of lock sync (although it's equally fine to recommend these users to turn it off, than vice versa).

So having it off by default for initial testing (with the intention of maybe changing this later) could make sense. On the flip side, you get less "testers" this way. In 3.x preserving backward compatibility was of utmost importance so defaulting to off makes sense.

> This could probably fix #58269 and make sync_to_physics obsolete. Despite the cool name, sync to physics is just a hack, a ugly one.

I'm not sure if physics interpolation makes Sync to Physics obsolete. The point of Sync to Physics is ensure that when a player is on a moving platform, the player won't lag behind the platform by 1 physics frame (and therefore appear to float over it when it moves downwards, or sink into it when it moves upwards). Enabling physics interpolation does not change how physics are calculated; it only changes how physics are *displayed*.

>
> 
> I'm not sure if physics interpolation makes Sync to Physics obsolete. The point of Sync to Physics is ensure that when a player is on a moving platform, the player won't lag behind the platform by 1 physics frame (and therefore appear to float over it when it moves downwards, or sink into it when it moves upwards). Enabling physics interpolation does not change how physics are calculated; it only changes how physics are _displayed_.

You are right. I was hoping it was just a visual thing.

Thanks @lawnjelly for the comments!

I've left the feature disabled by default, because enabling this on projects which are not made with this in mind can introduce streaking, and because particles and 3D are not done yet. We can revisit the default later. Let's ask people to test this on their 2D games in the release blog post and on social media.

With that I think this PR is ready to be merged, as soon as it can get a review.

`reset_physics_interpolation()` doesn't appear to be working for `PointLight2D`.
Not sure whether that is also the case in 3.x (it may be my mistake :grin: ).

EDIT: It's the same in 3.x, I'll try and work out why.

It's an order of operations bug, the transform notification is coming in _after_ the reset, even if the reset is called _after_ setting the transform in the script. I'll see if I can fix it in 3.x, and we can carry fix over.

Ok I have it:

The `Light2D` when calling `set_transform()` it updates the transform of the `canvas_item` immediately, however the light doesn't use this, instead uses a `canvas_light` RID and this only updates the `canvas_light_set_transform()` when a notification is received some time later.

This won't be too involved to fix but I can't guarantee I'll be able to do before going off on holiday tomorrow for a week, but I don't think this should be a showstopper for this PR (after all it is already merged in 3.x with this bug :smile: ).

This same bug could be affecting some of the other non-canvas items, but with any luck they can all be fixed in similar way.

UPDATE: Fixed in 3.x by #89577 . Should be fixed in this PR soon.
Thanks for the reviews! And thanks @markdibarry, it's done. This should be ready to merge now.

issue_context.title: Implement physics interpolation in 2D (already implemented in 3.x)
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v3.5.stable.official [991bb6ac7]

### System information

Mac OS X (Catalina) 10.15.7

### Issue description

Have a very simple parallax background and a moving RigidBody2D. It jitters every few seconds scrolling. I am just using add_force() once to get it going.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new scene with Node2D. 
2. Add ParallaxBackground and ParallaxLayer Texture background
3. Set the mirror to same size as Texture
4. Add a RigidBody2D with a Sprite, Camera and Collision2D
5. Check Camera2D as current
6. Add a force of 25 to Rigidbody2D
7. Run the project.
8. 

Notice that every few seconds the Spite snaps/jitters.



### Minimal reproduction project

Open and click run. Watch every few (maybe 10) seconds it bounces.

[ParallaxTest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9294200/ParallaxTest.zip)
comments:
Physics interpolation is not yet implemented for 2D. I'm aiming to have this working for 3.6.

Until then, feel free to try my addon which will do 2D interpolation:
https://github.com/lawnjelly/smoothing-addon
Drive by comment: I'm not certain physics interpolation is implemented in 4.0 at all (whether for 3D or 2D). Could this be clarified in docs?

review_comments:
If the goal is to do this before physics, why isn't it done before all physics (including 3D physics?)

It would make sense to me to open this up to 3D in the future, so either this should be moved before 3D, or the comment needs to be adjusted explaining why things are the way they are.

As-is, this code also leaves me with the question: If I want to disable 2D physics, should I keep this line enabled? I don't know.

@aaronfranke You are also absolutely right, I didn't spot this in the PR, the prepare should probably be before the 3D here (although it shouldn't make any difference until the 3D is done, so we can fix in 3D PR).

(This is actually something I need to double check in 3.x actually, because there was some rejigging here when I added 2D and it may have affected 3D, so thanks for pointing to this! :+1: 3.x has a `flush_queries()` here but no `sync()`.)

To address the confusion a little - "physics interpolation" (somewhat confusingly) is nothing to do with physics engine. The more correct name is fixed timestep interpolation.

The only relation is to the physics ticks, rather than the physics itself. It can work with or without physics engine. Juan preferred the name "physics interpolation", because even though incorrect, he thought it would be easier for users to understand (and admittedly in many cases their eyes would glaze over with "fixed timestep interpolation" :grin: ).

This is something that we as developers will be expected to learn the difference, but it will inevitably cause confusion in some way (if we e.g. called it "fixed timestep interpolation" in the c++, and "physics interpolation" for user facing code, this could be confusing, as many c++ funcs are bound etc, so it is called "physics interpolation" throughout).

As it is not related to the physics engines, it should not be disabled when disabling physics engines (as `_physics_process()` still occurs).

Just to try and explain what it is doing .. the `VisualServer` items have to be prepared before each iteration (tick) before any changes have been made to them (server side at least).

If you follow the code it calls `update_interpolation_tick()`.

This does a bunch of things:
* Detect any objects that are no longer being moved, and ensure their previous transform = current transform so they cease vibrating
* Store the current transform (from the last tick) to the previous transform, so they can be interpolated after the tick

Note: If you are doing snapping here, you may want the snapping to apply to the local object, but NOT to propagate to the children, so they can do their snapping independently. This may entail creating an extra intermediate e.g. `snapped_xform` and use this for rendering, while passing the unchanged `final_xform` to the children.

This certainly needs consideration because snapping is done differently in 3.x.
I tried multiple times snap the children independently (ask @markdibarry) but it always resulted with snapping issues. I think it's best to snap the parent as is and pass the parent to the children.

Just to note, this mentioned bug isn't introduced by physics interpolation, it is pre-existing, and this note is to remind to fix it, or make obvious if it appears in a later issue.

Fixing may need some care as `Camera2D` is pretty central to 2D games and there would be risk of regressions.

I got to think about godotengine/godot-cpp#1379 goal, and I think we can improve these lines by not initializing `xform` for nothing.

```suggestion
		Transform2D xform = is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()
				? _interpolation_data.xform_prev.interpolate_with(_interpolation_data.xform_curr, Engine::get_singleton()->get_physics_interpolation_fraction())
				: get_camera_transform();
```
